title: The Battle Before The Battle
subtitle: People Over Numbers
tagline: The people can be deteriorating while the institution appears to be thriving.
headline: People Over Numbers
seo_title: People Over Numbers: When Growth Hides the People
seo_description: Ezekiel 34 confronts shepherds who fed themselves and neglected the flock. Why growing numbers can hide exhausted people, and how leaders measure without forgetting them.
og_image_alt: People Over Numbers: The people can be deteriorating while the institution appears to be thriving. TheWrkShop, Leadership & Culture.

scriptures.text: Woe to you shepherds of Israel who only take care of yourselves! Should not shepherds take care of the flock?
You have not strengthened the weak or healed the sick or bound up the injured. You have not brought back the strays or searched for the lost.
You give a tenth of your spices—mint, dill and cumin. But you have neglected the more important matters of the law—justice, mercy and faithfulness.

blocks.text: God confronts Israel’s shepherds for caring for themselves while neglecting the flock.
They have failed to strengthen the weak, care for the sick, bind up the injured, and seek the straying.
Ezekiel 34 is not merely a criticism of ineffective leadership.
It is a confrontation over misplaced responsibility.
The shepherds have benefited from the flock without faithfully caring for it.
God names the specific people who have been neglected.
Notice how personal the indictment becomes.
GOD DOES NOT LET THE SHEPHERDS HIDE BEHIND THE SIZE OF THE FLOCK WHILE NEGLECTING THE CONDITION OF THE SHEEP.
That distinction matters for every leader.
An organization can be growing while the people inside it are deteriorating.
“IF OUR NUMBERS ARE IMPROVING, OUR PEOPLE MUST BE FLOURISHING.”
Imagine a ministry celebrating record attendance.
But beneath those numbers, some volunteers are exhausted.
Families feel overlooked.
Leaders are quietly burning out.
People who need care struggle to find it.
The growth may be genuine.
The accomplishments may matter.
But the numbers don’t tell the whole story.
WHAT WE COUNT CAN BE IMPORTANT WITHOUT BEING EVERYTHING THAT COUNTS.
Why do numbers become so powerful?
But numbers also offer something emotionally attractive.

items: Evidence that our sacrifices were worthwhile.

blocks.text: Eventually a leader may begin drawing personal worth from organizational performance.
Then declining numbers feel like personal failure.
And growing numbers feel like unquestionable approval.
THE DANGER BEGINS WHEN MEASUREMENT BECOMES IDENTITY.
Now the leader may resist any information that complicates the success story.
FAITHFUL STEWARDSHIP MEASURES RESULTS WITHOUT FORGETTING PEOPLE.
In Matthew 23:23, Jesus confronts religious leaders who carefully tithe their spices while neglecting justice, mercy, and faithfulness.
Busy is not the same as faithful.
He doesn’t condemn careful attention.
He corrects disordered priorities.
Likewise, Ezekiel doesn’t tell the shepherds to stop organizing or providing.
He confronts their failure to care.
Healthy organizations need both performance information and honest evidence about people’s well-being.
Growth should increase responsibility, not diminish attentiveness.

items: Who is exhausted, overlooked, or hurt while our numbers say we’re succeeding?
What do our dashboards reveal, and what do they conceal?
Are we measuring participation without examining spiritual formation?
Do people feel cared for, or merely needed?
What happens when someone’s well-being conflicts with a performance target?
Would we recognize success that came at an unacceptable human cost?

blocks.text: Review one celebrated metric.
Ask what it reveals and what it cannot reveal.
Listen to the people affected by the work.
Examine workload, care, development, and accountability.
Keep measuring what matters.
But refuse to let impressive numbers silence inconvenient human realities.
The people can be deteriorating while the institution appears to be thriving.

Father, forgive us where success has become more important than stewardship. Give us eyes for the overlooked, the exhausted, and the hurting. Teach us to celebrate growth without neglecting care. May every person entrusted to us matter more than the appearance of success. In Jesus’ name, Amen.
What we count can be important without being everything that counts.
Growth should increase responsibility, not diminish attentiveness.
Measurement becomes dangerous when it becomes identity.
Never let a successful report become an excuse to overlook a suffering person.
